props.gloss_en: the baraita: one who walks in a place of bands of wild beasts and robbers prays a short prayer
R' Eliezer: 'Do Your will in the heavens above, and give ease of spirit to those who fear You below, and do what is good in Your eyes. Blessed are You, Lord, who hears prayer'
R' Yehoshua: 'Hear the cry of Your people Israel, and quickly do their request. Blessed are You, Lord, who hears prayer'
R' Elazar b. R' Tzadok: 'Hear the outcry of Your people Israel, and quickly do their request. Blessed are You, Lord, who hears prayer'

Acherim: 'The needs of Your people Israel are many and their understanding is short; may it be Your will, Lord our God, to give each one his sustenance and each body what it lacks. Blessed are You, Lord, who hears prayer'
Rav Huna: the halakha follows Acherim
Eliyahu: do not grow angry, and you will not sin
Eliyahu: do not get drunk, and you will not sin
Eliyahu: and when you go out on the road, consult your Maker and go out
Rav Chisda: 'consult your Maker and go out' -- this is the traveller's prayer
Rav Chisda: anyone who goes out on the road must pray the traveller's prayer

what is the traveller's prayer? 'May it be Your will, Lord my God, that You lead me toward peace, direct my steps toward peace, support me toward peace, rescue me from every enemy and ambush on the way, send blessing in the work of my hands, and grant me grace, kindness and mercy in Your eyes and in the eyes of all who see me. Blessed are You, Lord, who hears prayer'
Abaye: always a person should join himself with the congregation
Abaye: how should he say it? 'May it be Your will, Lord our God, that You lead us toward peace', etc.
Rav Chisda: [when does he pray it?] from the time he walks on the road
Rav Chisda: [until how much?] until a parasang
Rav Chisda: [how does he pray it?] standing
Rav Sheshet: even walking
Rav Chisda, walking on the road with Rav Sheshet, stood and prayed (the narrator; and the attendant: he is standing and praying)
Rav Sheshet to his attendant: stand me up too and I will pray
Rav Sheshet: from being good, do not be called bad
havinenu: he must pray the first three and the last three [blessings]
havinenu: and when he reaches his home he need not pray again
the short prayer: he need pray neither the first three nor the last three
the short prayer: and when he reaches his home he must pray again
the halakha: havinenu -- standing
the short prayer -- whether standing or walking
